title: CI sentinels: plan/apply gates, OPA evidence, and upgrade health checks
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
Implement a robust CI 'sentinel' layer for Terraform-based Private (VPC) deployments that combines linting, plan gating, OPA/Conftest policy evidence, and automated health checks to make upgrades and routine applies safe and observable. This ticket delivers the CI workflows, policy adapters, and a lightweight health prober that runs post-apply smoke checks to catch resource drift, IAM regressions, and KMS/access boundary misconfigurations before and after rollout.

Context and motivation:
- Customers running Redwood Private require predictable, auditable, and reversible infra changes. We currently lack a unified CI pipeline that enforces policy-as-code, surface-level cost/impact annotations, and post-deploy health probes for the VPC modules used by Private customers.
- Existing ad-hoc pipelines leave too much manual review burden on platform engineers and increase blast radius during module upgrades. A sentinels layer (lint -> plan gate -> automated scanning -> plan evidence -> controlled apply -> post-apply health checks) reduces mean time to detect and rollback unsafe changes.

Scope / deliverables:
1) CI pipeline templates (GitHub Actions + Terraform Cloud/Enterprise workflow examples) that: lint (terraform fmt + tflint), run static security scans (conftest/OPA + tfsec or checkov), generate structured plan artifacts (terraform plan --out + JSON), and upload policy evidence to S3/GCS or the console for audit.
2) A Conftest/OPA policy bundle for our VPC modules that includes checks for: public subnet misconfigurations, IAM policy size/escape-clauses, KMS key usage, resource tagging, and prohibited resource types. Each rule should map to a remediation hint and severity.
3) A Plan Evidence Adapter: small script/action that converts terraform plan JSON into a normalized evidence artifact (summary, changed resources list, resource counts, estimated new costs) and attaches policy results (pass/fail + failing rule IDs). Integrates with PR comments and the Console's audit ingestion endpoint.
4) Apply gating strategy: a default "blocked" gate on PRs with policy failures; a stage gate for canary applies to a single workspace/environment for major module changes; automated rollback triggers if post-apply health checks fail.
5) Post-apply health prober that runs smoke checks for newly applied infra: verifies VPC subnets exist and route table consistency, checks that expected security groups allow egress to our telemetry endpoints, confirms KMS key policies have expected principals, and runs a simple connectivity test to private endpoints. Health prober reports must be structured and stored for 30 days.
6) Documentation: runbook for on-call, PR templates, policy authoring guide, and examples for repository-level pipeline configuration.

Acceptance criteria:
- CI template is merged and used by 2 internal repos (private-bootstrap, infra-modules).
- Conftest bundle has at least 18 rules with automated unit tests and sample fixtures.
- Plan Evidence artifacts are viewable in PRs and the Console ingest path accepts the artifact schema.
- Post-apply prober runs automatically in the apply workflow and returns pass/fail with logs; a failing probe triggers a documented rollback playbook.
- Security review completed and sign-off from compliance.

Design decisions and trade-offs considered:
- We evaluated running OPA in a centralized policy engine vs local Conftest checks. Chosen approach: policy-as-code runs in CI via Conftest (fast failure feedback) with optional centralized re-evaluation in a policy service for long-term audit and cross-repo enforcement. This balances developer velocity with enterprise auditability.
- For plan artifacts we standardize on terraform plan JSON as the canonical source, but include a small normalization layer so that different Terraform versions produce consistent evidence.
- Post-apply health checks are intentionally lightweight (non-destructive) to avoid flapping resources; deeper validations remain on the on-call playbook and periodic drift jobs.

Work breakdown (initial implementation):
- Spike (2d): prototype Conftest rules against private-bootstrap module (Aisha) — DONE.
- Pipeline template (3d): GH Action + Terraform Cloud example + secrets handling (Marco) — IN PROGRESS.
- Plan Evidence Adapter (3d): normalize plan JSON, generate summary + cost rough estimate (TBD) — IN PROGRESS.
- Post-apply prober (4d): small Go binary/step that runs configured checks and posts results — TODO.
- Tests & fixtures (4d): unit tests for policies, end-to-end runbook validation in staging workspace — TODO.
- Docs & runbook (2d): PR templates, escalation steps — TODO.

Open questions / blockers:
- KMS key principal lists: we need a canonical source of truth for expected principals in Private deployments. (Blocked until infra-security team provides the list.)
- Terraform version pinning: we need to decide which minimum TF versions to support in the normalization adapter. Recommendation: 1.5+; confirm with infra.
- Storage/location for evidence artifacts and retention policy (S3 vs internal Console ingest). Need compliance input on retention.

Links / artifacts:
- Spike notes: drive.redwood/internal/private-spikes/ci-sentinels-2025-11
- Conftest rules proto: github.com/redwood/infra-modules/tree/ci-sentinels/conftest
- Example GH Action: github.com/redwood/infra-actions/terraform-plan-evidence
- Runbook draft: docs/internal/terraform-ci-sentinels.md

Rollout plan:
1) Merge CI templates behind feature flag; require on all module PRs in internal repos.
2) Run for one month in report-only mode (policy results posted to PRs but not blocking) to surface false positives.
3) Adjust rules, then flip gates to block for critical severity.
4) Enable post-apply prober for canary workspaces and measure rollback rate.

Risks and mitigation:
- False positives in OPA rules: mitigate with report-only phase and test fixtures.
- Pipeline runtime/perf: lint and conftest run in parallel; heavy cost estimation moved offline.
- State drift/locking across multiple workspaces: ensure our workspace per-environment guidance and remote state locking are enforced by templates.

Next steps (short term):
- unblock KMS principals list with infra-security (owner: Marco)
- land Conftest bundle + unit tests (owner: Aisha)
- finish GH Action template and upload artifact schema to Console ingest (owner: Marco)
